survivingClaim: Precise obstruction, confirmed. For finite P and H holomorphic with Re H >= 0 on the polydisc, the weighted first moment of zeta over the poles of a lossless h = H((p^{-z})) is (T/2pi)(H(0) + conj h(1/2)) + o(T), with real part at least (T/2pi) Re H(0). So no such h other than an imaginary constant can be split off xi'/xi as a positive-real summand (Theorem B; its hypothesis implies RH, its proof does not assume it). No bounded multi-delay factor divides S (trivial, from gamma growth). Within the unipotent chain family the joint defect is rank one and additive, so joint contractivity is the scalar inequality Re U_P <= Re G and twists are torus translations. The sharp joint section fails at fixed sigma < 1 for all large Q by the pole term (classical). The Fejer-tapered section is an explicit-formula identity equivalent to RH that uses no multiplicativity; its measured separation of zeta from twists holds at sigma = 1/2 on the windows tried and is window-dependent at sigma = 0.6. Infinite P, general J-inner sections and the DH analogue remain open. No progress on RH and no statement about zeros of zeta.
obstruction: Within the unipotent chain family a block of prime sections has rank-one additive J-defect, so joint contractivity is the scalar inequality Re U_P <= Re G and twists are torus translations. For finite P no positive-real function of several prime delays can be split off xi'/xi (Theorem B). The sharp section fails at fixed sigma < 1 for large Q (pole term). The Fejer-tapered section is an explicit-formula identity equivalent to RH that uses no multiplicativity. Open: infinite P, general J-inner linear-fractional sections, DH analogue.
controlsThatDefeat: sign and unimodular twists (torus translations; fail at the same prime as zeta at sigma = 1/2 in the sharp section)
tapered section separates zeta from twists only as an RH-equivalent identity; separation is window-dependent at sigma = 0.6
lesson: Sections of the prime chain commute and have rank-one additive defect, so grouping primes adds no freedom: joint contractivity is the largest-value inequality itself. What separates zeta's phases from twists is one-sidedness of the prime sum coming from the zero measure via the functional equation (visible with Fejer weights), not Kronecker structure of finitely many primes; that is a restatement of RH. Multiplicativity entered only in a no-go (point evaluation of H at p^-1/2).
followUp: Referee Theorem A step (iii) (off-diagonal and horizontal error terms; checked numerically to 1-3 percent at T=6000 only), then update row Q12 and item 7 of the obstruction map. The remaining open case is a J-inner linear-fractional section in several delays with Theta(0)=M(c0)U0, c0>0. No server run needed; none was used.
